clue.text: Request to be the church of the diocese

parts.note: taken as written
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: Someone asks to become the cathedral church of a diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the church before the diocese; read 'the church of the diocese' as the diocese's own church, so the diocese comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to implore or beg, a stronger synonym of the verb request.

clue.text: My idea is to be going round in an old aircraft

indicators.note: going round means the letters of be surround the phrase

parts.note: taken as written
my idea is put as 'I plan'

explanation.surface: Someone's ambition is to circle about in a vintage aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My idea is to' reads as 'I plan to'; 'going round' puts BE around I PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An early aeroplane with two pairs of wings stacked one above the other, typical of the First World War era.

clue.text: Fish? Goat? One dozen about possible

definitions.text: Fish? Goat? One dozen about possible

parts.words: Fish? Goat? One dozen about possible
parts.note: Pisces the fish and Capricorn the goat are two of the twelve possible astrological signs

explanation.walkthrough: The fish and the goat are astrological creatures, and there are a dozen such signs to choose from.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisces and Capricorn are among the twelve divisions of the astrological year.

clue.text: Braun's talk about love will vanish into thin air

parts.note: Eva Braun was Hitler's companion

indicators.note: about means the word for talk is wrapped round the zero

parts.note: to prate is to talk foolishly
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O

explanation.surface: Eva Braun's chatter about romance will disappear without trace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside PRATE to give PORATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to turn into vapour, and so figuratively to disappear completely.

clue.text: A place for the shade?

parts.note: a shade is a ghost of the dead in classical myth, so the clue asks where such spirits are kept

explanation.walkthrough: The clue suggests a cool spot out of the sun, but a shade is a departed spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek underworld is the dwelling of the spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Celebrity status as Mr Tod contrived it

indicators.note: contrived means put together artfully, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fox from Beatrix Potter, Mr Tod, schemes his way to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Tod is the fox in a Beatrix Potter tale; here he is just seven letters (with AS) to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being a star, the position of fame enjoyed by a celebrity.

clue.text: Educational scene: beginners took precedence in the timetable

parts.note: the beginnings of school, the educational scene, and of educational, SCH and EDU
led means went first, took precedence

explanation.surface: In a school, the youngest pupils come first on the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of SCHool and EDUcational give SCHEDU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scheduled has been entered in the timetable for a set time.

clue.text: Suggest a rise for the storyteller

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the letters run upwards, so they are read backwards

parts.note: to pose a question is to put forward or suggest it

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a pay rise for the narrator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' looks like a pay rise but turns POSE A upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of moral fables.

clue.text: Finance-led policy drama resulting under puppet

parts.note: a doll is a puppet-like toy figure

indicators.note: resulting signals that the letters are reworked into an outcome

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A policy shaped by money ends in a drama controlled by a puppet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resulting' reworks POLICY DRAMA into ARDIPLOMACY, which goes 'under' DOLL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a foreign policy driven by loans and investment, so it is diplomacy led by finance.

clue.text: Rubber reported by my sister in Paris?

indicators.note: reported means the French phrase is heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: ma soeur is French for my sister

explanation.surface: Gossip passed on by a French nun about someone who gives massages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' looks like the material, but it is someone who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gives massages rubs the muscles of his clients.

clue.text: Pork sandwich — missing fragment is replaced lest it should comes

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Pork sandwich — missing fragment is replaced lest it should comes', is garbled at the end ('it should comes'), so neither the definition nor which letters are replaced can be pinned down.
annotationWithheld.clue: Pork sandwich — missing fragment is replaced lest it should comes

clue.text: With final change on top from the start

indicators.note: the final change tells us to alter the last letter of the word for on top

parts.note: above means on top, higher up

explanation.surface: Something arrives with a last-minute alteration at the top, right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the last letter E of ABOVE to O, giving the Latin phrase meaning 'from the egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, literally from the egg, is used in English to mean from the very beginning.

clue.text: Team on river could have a roll here

parts.note: a side is a sports team
the River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.surface: A sports team out on a river might take a roll, as in a boat capsizing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' suggests a boat rolling on the water, but it is a bread roll, served on the small plate beside a diner's main one.
explanation.definitionFit: A small plate set at the side of a place setting is where a bread roll is put at dinner.

clue.text: Put constraints on much of programme during Lent, possibly

indicators.note: during means one thing sits within the span of another, here inside the shuffled letters
possibly signals that the letters of Lent might be arranged another way
much of means most but not all, so the opening of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone restricts a broadcast schedule during the Lenten season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LENT as ENTL; 'much of' drops the first four letters of programme; 'during' places what is left between ENT and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrammel is to entangle or hamper, an old verb meaning to restrict as with a net.

clue.text: Heartless character losing direction in planet at the end of World War I

definitions.text: the end of World War I

indicators.note: in means the shortened character is put inside the planet

parts.note: Mars is the red planet

indicators.note: losing means the compass point is dropped

parts.note: the Tin Man in The Wizard of Oz has no heart
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A heartless figure loses his way on a planet at the close of the Great War.
explanation.walkthrough: Armistice Day, 11 November 1918, fell on St Martin's feast day.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian feast of St Martin falls on 11 November, the date of the 1918 Armistice.

clue.text: Treat as a dogsbody RUC man backing lawyers on strike

parts.note: Sir Hugh Orde was Chief Constable of the Northern Ireland police that succeeded the RUC

indicators.note: backing here means the word for lawyers is read from right to left

parts.note: the Bar is the body of barristers, lawyers collectively
workers on strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish policeman supports striking lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police force; 'backing' looks like support but reverses BAR to RAB.
explanation.definitionFit: To order someone about is to boss them with constant commands, treating them as a drudge.

clue.text: Concerned with a profit another time

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: Worrying about making money, someone repeats the exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something once more means repeating it on a later occasion.

clue.text: Note to vicar: get a life outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for existing goes round the cleric's title

parts.note: to have life is simply to be, to exist
Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a vicar

explanation.surface: A memo to a clergyman telling him to go out and enjoy himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written memo but is the musical note; 'get a life' is a slangy taunt standing for BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a long musical note, equal in length to two semibreves.

clue.text: A quiz night without a quiz? Hardly on the cards

definitions.text: A quiz night without a quiz? Hardly on the cards

parts.words: A quiz night without a quiz? Hardly on the cards
parts.note: a social gathering with games but no questions is a card evening, so the event is literally on the cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly on the cards' looks like 'unlikely', but this card game is literally played with cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for two players using a pack of 64 cards, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Plant to stimulate the left?

parts.note: Reds are those on the political left
a pepper is read as something that peps up, stimulating

explanation.surface: A political agent planted to energise the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests an infiltrator in politics, but it is the capsicum.
explanation.definitionFit: The capsicum grown for its sweet scarlet fruit is a plant as well as a vegetable.

clue.text: Rubber done 14 down to be rendered into heater?

definitions.text: Rubber done 14 down to be rendered into heater?

parts.words: Rubber done 14 down to be rendered into heater?
parts.note: the rubber is a tyre given a fresh tread a second time; worn tyres also get burnt as fuel

explanation.walkthrough: '14 down' refers to another entry, meaning 'once more'; the tyre's rubber is redone rather than melted down.
explanation.definitionFit: An old tyre with new tread moulded on is reused rubber, given a second life.

clue.text: I study animals and see soldiers going into Australia from the East

indicators.note: going here means the soldiers travel inside the run of letters around them
in an across clue, from the East means read right to left

parts.note: into is given by its synonym to
Oz is the informal name for Australia
lo is an old word meaning see or behold
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A scientist says that he notes troops heading into Australia from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into Australia' is TO OZ, which 'from the East' turns into ZOOT; 'going' sends the see-and-soldiers letters inside, after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who researches animal life speaks in the first person here.

clue.text: Award for 4x4?

parts.note: a 4x4 is a big vehicle; OS stands for outsize
a 4x4 is a car

explanation.surface: Is there a prize for the best off-road vehicle?
explanation.walkthrough: A 4x4 is a four-wheel-drive vehicle, read as an outsize (OS) car.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette given for film achievement is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Light piece for light orchestra

indicators.note: a piece is a part of a whole, so a run of letters is taken from inside the words

explanation.surface: A short light work written for a light orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like a musical piece but takes letters from the middle of 'light orchestra'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-held electric lamp, or a flaming brand, is a portable light.

clue.text: See 14
Preserve carpenter and spoil the sick man of Europe

parts.note: Peter Quince is the carpenter among the mechanicals in A Midsummer Night's Dream
to mar is to spoil
malade is French for sick, so the sick person of a European tongue

explanation.surface: A carpenter and a ruined invalid, the old Ottoman 'sick man of Europe', make a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sick man of Europe' was a nickname for the Ottoman Empire, but here it is just French for 'sick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam made from the fruit of the quince tree is a preserve.

clue.text: People from Aberdeenshire about right as accompanists

indicators.note: about means the people go round the abbreviation

parts.note: Aberdeenshire lies in the east of Scotland, so its folk are E(ast) Scots

explanation.surface: Scots from the north-east are said to be good at accompanying others.
explanation.walkthrough: Aberdeenshire is a county in north-east Scotland, so its people are East Scots, E SCOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: People who escort others go along with them, so they are companions or accompanists.

clue.text: Sharpened, including what used to be the sweet

indicators.note: including means the archaic word sits inside the word for sharpened

parts.note: honed means sharpened, as a blade
ye is the old written form of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: A blade is sharpened, taking in what was once a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like a noun, a dessert, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeyed words are sweet and flattering, as if coated with honey.
